clue.text: Wonder if vehicle has turned back within eight furlongs

indicators.note: within says the turned vehicle sits inside the distance

parts.note: eight furlongs make one mile

indicators.note: a vehicle that has turned back is read from right to left

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A racegoer marvels at whether a car could turn round inside a mile of track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has turned back' turns CAR into RAC, and 'within' puts it inside MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel or prodigy is something that makes you wonder, an event beyond nature.

clue.text: First movement intending to be disabling

indicators.note: First takes only the opening letter of movement

parts.note: aiming means intending

explanation.surface: A composer's first movement is meant to cripple the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First movement' looks like music but gives only M.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to wound or cripple, so this is crippling.

clue.text: Dashed, on finding account overdrawn

indicators.note: finding here means the outer word finds the other inside it

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off on discovering their bank balance is negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' puts AC inside RED; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushed or sped along; to race is to run quickly.

clue.text: Fast asleep, so came to grief

indicators.note: came to grief means the words before it are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone fell deeply asleep and so ended up in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grief' rearranges SO CAME TO; 'Fast' means deeply, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep unconsciousness is the medical state of a coma, here used for heavy slumber.

clue.text: In revenge you aim to get it

indicators.note: In tells us the answer is tucked inside the next word

explanation.surface: Seeking revenge, you aim to get your own back.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'revenge', and to get it is what an avenger wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting square or level with someone who wronged you is the aim of the idiom 'get' plus this word.

clue.text: Redeploy one column unless it's for the quiz

indicators.note: to redeploy is to arrange afresh, so the letters are shuffled
read as UN less: the letters U and N are taken away from the words before them

explanation.surface: Military orders to move a column of troops, with a strange exception for a quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unless' splits as UN + less, removing U and N from ONECOLUMN to leave ONECOLM, which 'Redeploy' rearranges. 'Quiz' is an old word for an eyeglass, the quizzing glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A quizzing glass was a single eyeglass for peering at things, so the lens is what one used to quiz.

clue.text: Claim triad responsible against keeping mum!

indicators.note: responsible is a rare anagram signal; the words are reshaped into what they cause

explanation.surface: A Hong Kong gang is accused of killing a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible' rearranges CLAIM TRIAD. 'Keeping mum' looks like staying quiet but here means keeping mother alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing one's own mother is the crime, so someone so inclined opposes letting mother live.

clue.text: One way to get Susan a situation abroad

indicators.note: one way to get the letters is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A travel tip on how Susan can find a job overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way to get' rearranges SUSAN and A into the capital of the Bahamas.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the Bahamas is a place, a location, outside Britain.

clue.text: Such a din! Arch collapsed on poor Ravi, understand

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Such a din! Arch collapsed on poor Ravi, understand'. Anagrams of ARCH and RAVI give eight letters; the final I needs a word such as 'I' that the feed lacks, and 'understand' cannot supply it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Such a din! Arch collapsed on poor Ravi, understand

clue.text: Outlay for swans banker housed

indicators.note: housed means the birds are lodged inside the river

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Exe is a river in Devon
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: A bank spends money on swans for its premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river (it has banks): the EXE in Devon, England. 'housed' puts PENS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Money laid out on something is a cost or expenditure.

clue.text: Obligatory to show flair, first putting in ground cumin

indicators.note: the rearranged spice is put in first, before the flair
cumin seeds are ground in a mill, so the word's letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: a bent is a natural flair or talent

explanation.surface: A cook shows off by adding ground cumin first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns CUMIN into INCUM; 'first putting in' places it ahead of BENT. 'Ground' looks like a cooking step but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incumbent on you is a duty you are obliged to carry out.

clue.text: The trophy someone failed to keep under lock?

definitions.text: The trophy someone failed to keep under lock?

parts.words: The trophy someone failed to keep under lock?
parts.note: a victor's trophy taken from a beaten foe, which is also the skin that sits beneath a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A prize was stolen because nobody kept it locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a secure door, but it is a lock of hair; the skin under it was taken as a trophy by warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors cut the skin of the head from beaten enemies as a trophy, and that skin lies under the hair.

clue.text: Compose something — it turns out to be too short for editing

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters coming out in a fresh order
a word that is too short has lost its last letter

explanation.surface: A writer finds a piece is too short to bother editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too short' cuts the G off EDITING, leaving EDITIN, and 'turns out' rearranges it. 'something' and 'to be ... for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite is an old word meaning to write or put into words, as a letter or poem.

clue.text: Crazy action — it gets official commendation

indicators.note: crazy means the letters go wild and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: Someone does something mad and is praised for it officially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges ACTION and IT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal mention in dispatches praising bravery is a soldier's official tribute.

clue.text: Newspaper spread on double bed

definitions.meaning: a full-size newspaper as opposed to a tabloid
a wide sheet laid over a big bed

explanation.surface: A newspaper is spread out across a double bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The large-format paper and a wide bedsheet share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-format paper, and literally a wide piece of bed linen.

clue.text: A healthy breed of rolling stock?

definitions.meaning: a sound, healthy line of animals or plants
railway wagons carrying freight; split the letters 5,5 and they name a freight train

explanation.surface: A railway joke: a sturdy pedigree of locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way the letters make a fine breed; move the space one letter on and they make a freight train.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthy describes a good line of descent, while freight wagons on the railway form a train carrying goods.

clue.text: Travelling? Do another detour

indicators.note: a detour sends the letters by a different route

explanation.surface: A driver is told to take yet another diversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detour' rearranges DO ANOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone journeying is out and about, the idiom for being away on a trip.

clue.text: Disturb a somnambulist on this path?

definitions.meaning: to rouse a sleepwalker from sleep
the track of disturbed water left behind a moving ship

explanation.surface: A warning not to rouse a sleepwalker as they cross your path.
explanation.walkthrough: The trail a boat leaves in the water is the second sense; 'on this' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse from sleep, and the trail left in water behind a vessel.

clue.text: Its bark getting con-man in trouble?

definitions.note: the clue names the bark of a tree; the answer is the spice made from that bark

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A dog's bark lands a swindler in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges CON-MAN IN. 'bark' suggests a dog but is tree bark.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice comes from the dried inner bark of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Foreign lawyer gets thanks for information

parts.note: DA, District Attorney, is an American prosecutor, foreign to a British solver
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: An overseas lawyer is thanked for passing on facts.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for study are the plural Latin word for things given.

clue.text: The female side of underworld river

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
the Taff is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Women from beside an infernal river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff flows through Cardiff in Wales; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The spindle-staff was women's work, so it stands for the maternal branch of a family.

clue.text: A tit flies recklessly, with a lethal outcome

definitions.note: singular in the clue, but the answer is the plural count of deaths that such an outcome brings

indicators.note: recklessly shows the bird's letters flying about wildly

explanation.surface: A small bird flies about carelessly and comes to a sad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recklessly' rearranges A TIT FLIES together with the A after 'with', which joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaths in an accident are counted as the toll of a deadly event.

clue.text: Intend to round pier-head in this vessel

parts.note: shall expresses intention
a round shape is the letter O
the head of the word pier is P

explanation.surface: A sailor plans to steer around the end of the pier in his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pier-head' gives the first letter of pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open boat or small sloop is a kind of craft.

clue.text: Woodland gods almost mute, I found

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: mute means silent

explanation.surface: Someone finds forest deities nearly speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SILENT to SILEN, then I is added; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These were drunken old satyr-like companions of Bacchus in classical myth, spirits of the forest.

clue.text: Observe change of diets necessary for those most unwell

parts.note: to observe is to see

indicators.note: a change of diets means its letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A doctor advises patients who feel worst to look at changing their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges DIETS into DIEST, after SEE. 'necessary for those' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy is informal for poorly or off-colour, so the superlative is sickest.

clue.text: In bad trouble? A conference is called for

indicators.note: trouble shakes up the two words before it

explanation.surface: When things go badly, a meeting must be called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IN BAD into INDAB, then A follows. The answer is a word from southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a southern African council or meeting of tribal leaders to discuss problems.

clue.text: Alien rear in ventilator

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Alien rear in ventilator'. No parse gives the five letters: an anagram of REAR lacks an I, and REAR plus IN has six letters; a word appears lost in the feed.

clue.text: Boy the girl married

parts.note: she is the girl

explanation.surface: The boy the girl married.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a son of Noah in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's eldest son in Genesis is a male given name.

clue.text: Are about to act as lovers do

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the next

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: Lovers behave in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DO inside ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers worship and cherish one another, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Real Eastern hemp gone up in smoke!

definitions.text: Real Eastern hemp gone up in smoke!

indicators.note: the material burns and scatters, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern

explanation.surface: Genuine oriental cannabis has been smoked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone up in smoke' rearranges REAL, E and HEMP; the whole clue also describes something that lasted only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke vanishes in a moment, which is exactly what fleeting, short-lived things do.

clue.text: With clenched knuckles holding supplement, is slave to his hobby

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the other inside it

parts.note: knuckles clenched together form a fist
to add is to supplement

explanation.surface: A man with clenched fists clings to his supplements, obsessed with his hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts ADD inside FIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows a craze or fad obsessively is a devotee of a passing pursuit.

clue.text: Gin not only mother's ruin?

parts.note: gin is a snare as well as the drink called mother's ruin; this snare catches people, and the term also means a seductive woman, a ruin for men

explanation.surface: Gin ruins more than just mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTHER'S RUIN is British slang for gin; but a gin is also a trap, and this one is set for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare, and a snare for catching trespassers or a woman who ensnares men fits both senses.
